On September 5, 2023, Liam Novak, a 68-year-old male patient, presented to the Emergency Department at St. Francis Hospital with severe abdominal pain that started approximately 12 hours prior to arrival. The pain was described as sharp and constant, localized in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen.

HPI: Mr. Novak reported no recent changes in diet or bowel habits but mentioned a history of cholelithiasis (gallstones) diagnosed 5 years ago. He denied any fever, chills, or jaundice but did endorse some nausea without vomiting.

PE: On physical examination by Dr. Haruki Sato, Liam was found to be in moderate distress due to pain. Vital signs were within normal limits except for a slightly elevated blood pressure at 148/90 mmHg. Abdominal exam revealed tenderness in the right upper quadrant with positive Murphy's sign.

Diagnostic Findings:
1. Laboratory results showed mild leukocytosis with WBC count of 12,000/mm³ and elevated liver enzymes (ALT: 120 U/L and AST: 95 U/L).
2. An abdominal ultrasound confirmed the presence of multiple gallstones with a thickened gallbladder wall indicative of acute cholecystitis.

Course of Treatment:
1. Liam was admitted for management of acute cholecystitis.
2. He was kept NPO (nothing by mouth), started on IV fluids and antibiotics (Ceftriaxone and Metronidazole).
3. A surgical consult was requested; after evaluation by the surgical team led by Drs. Jessica Brown and Amir Patel, a decision was made to perform a laparoscopic cholecystectomy which occurred without complications on September 6th.

Postoperative Period:
Mr Novak tolerated the procedure well; he was started on clear liquids post-op day one which he tolerated without issue advancing to regular diet afterwards.
Pain control achieved with Acetaminophen & short course IV morphine transitioning Oral oxycodone as needed
He will be discharged home once passing flatus & tolerating oral intake
with prescriptions for oral analgesics & instructions regarding wound care 
Follow up appointment scheduled in General Surgery clinic within one week

Discharge Date: September 8th

Assisting medical team included internist Dr Anders Lindqvist along w nursing staff members RN Rebecca Levy & Dina Petrova LPN

Diagnosis: Acute left ureteral colic secondary to obstructing renal stone.

Treatment:
1) IV hydration with Lactated Ringer's solution
2) Analgesia with IV morphine sulfate
3) Antiemetic ondansetron administered for nausea
4) Tamsulosin initiated for medical expulsion therapy

Urology consult recommended outpatient follow-up within one week and provided patient education materials regarding kidney stones through their online portal (https://patient.nm.org).

Mr.Novak was discharged home after adequate analgesia was achieved with prescriptions for oral analgesics and instructions to strain urine for stone passage.

His wife reported that he had been experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath for the past week. Patient contact: (917) 555-0198. Email: m.sokolov@email.com. Address: 123 W 74th St, Apt 5B, New York, NY 10023. Medical Record Number: NYP-1029384756.

Dr. Sunil Patel admitted Mr. Sokolov for further evaluation and management of suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The patient underwent several diagnostic tests:

1. Electrocardiogram (ECG): Sinus tachycardia with non-specific ST-segment changes
2. Troponin levels: Elevated at 0.52 ng/mL (normal range <0.04 ng/mL)
3. Echocardiogram: Mild left ventricular hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 45%

Based on these findings and his clinical presentation, Mr.Sokolov was diagnosed with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). He was started on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol tartrate, lisinopril therapy per ACS protocol.

A cardiac catheterization revealed significant stenoses in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) and right coronary artery (RCA). Two drug-eluting stents were successfully implanted by Dr.Patel using the Philips Azurion image-guided therapy platform.

Mr.Sokolov's condition improved post-intervention; he was discharged on January 10th with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy(DAPT) for at least one year alongside his antihypertensive medications.

Follow-up appointments:
1.Cardiac rehabilitation intake assessment - January17th
2.Outpatient cardiology visit - February7th

Patient education materials regarding lifestyle modifications post-MI were provided through https://www.nyp.org/heart-health along with instructions to enroll in NYP's online patient portal MyChart(https://mychart.nyp.org/mychart).

His contact information is as follows: phone (310) 555-2468, address 1234 Sunset Blvd Apt 5B, Los Angeles, CA 90046. The hospital can be reached via their website at https://www.uclahealth.org/. Liam's email is liam.novak@email.com and his health plan ID is UCLAH-654321.

Upon arrival at the hospital, medical staff noted that Mr. Novak was unconscious and had an irregular pulse. The attending physician Dr. Ramon Lee ordered an EKG which revealed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. An IV was started and diltiazem was administered to control the heart rate.

Once stabilized, Mr. Novak regained consciousness and reported feeling lightheaded earlier in the day but did not seek medical attention until he collapsed in his kitchen around noon. He also mentioned missing his last two doses of metformin due to a recent change in his medication schedule.

Dr. Lee admitted Mr. Novak for observation overnight in the telemetry unit for continuous cardiac monitoring using a Philips IntelliVue MX40 wearable patient monitor (Serial No: PH98765). Additional tests including cardiac enzymes and a transthoracic echocardiogram were ordered to rule out any underlying cardiac issues that may have contributed to his collapse.

After reviewing all test results which came back within normal limits on September 6th post-admission day one; Dr Lee diagnosed Mr.Novak with uncontrolled atrial fibrillation secondary to medication noncompliance likely exacerbated by his preexisting conditions of HTN & DM2 . Discharge instructions included resuming metformin as previously prescribed along with starting apixaban for stroke prevention given his CHA2DS2-VASc score >2 . F/u appointment scheduled w/ cardiology clinic in one week .

 Patient education materials provided about managing chronic conditions like DM & importance of medication adherence , overview of afib including symptoms / red flags plus when seek prompt medical care via ED or PCP . Thank you for your assistance in managing this complex case.

Best regards,

Dr. Emily Davis

On September 5, 2023, Liam Novak, a 68-year-old male patient, presented to the neurology clinic with a history of chronic migraines and recent onset of unilateral numbness and tingling in his right arm.

HPI: Mr. Novak has been experiencing intermittent headaches for the past 20 years, typically occuring 2-3 times per month and lasting for several hours. The headaches are described as throbbing and are usually located in the temporal regions bilaterally. Over-the-counter analgesics provide mild relief. However, two weeks ago he developed persistent numbness and tingling sensation in his right arm extending from his shoulder to his fingertips. The symptoms have not improved with NSAIDs or rest.

PE: On examination, Mr. Novak appeared uncomfortable but not in acute distress. Cranial nerves II-XII were intact bilaterally without deficits. Motor strength was normal (5/5) throughout all extremities except for mild weakness (4/5) noted in the right upper extremity with wrist extension and grip strength. Sensation was diminished to light touch and pinprick over the right C6-C8 dermatomes compared to the left side.

Diagnostic studies:
1. MRI brain without contrast - No acute intracranial abnormalities identified.
2. MRI cervical spine without contrast - Moderate foraminal stenosis at C5-C6 level on the right side secondary to uncovertebral joint hypertrophy resulting in compression of the exiting C6 nerve root.
3 . EMG/NCS - Evidence of chronic right C6 radiculopathy corresponding with imaging findings.

Diagnosis: Chronic migraine headache disorder; Right C6 cervical radiculopathy due to foraminal stenosis

Treatment plan:
1 . Continue current migraine prophylaxis regimen (propranolol 80mg daily), add gabapentin starting at 300mg nightly for neuropathic pain related to radiculopathy
2 . Referral made for physical therapy focusing on cervical stabilization exercises 
3 . Neurosurgery consult scheduled on October 10th to discuss possible surgical intervention options 
4 . Follow up appointment scheduled with neurology clinic after completion of PT course or sooner if symptoms worsen

2) Podiatry assessment in two weeks
3) Endocrinology consult as needed

2) Aspirin desensitization protocol commenced as per standard hospital policy.

1) Pre-procedure timeout completed following universal protocol guidelines.
2) Transradial approach right heart catheterization performed by Dr.Hakimi under fluoroscopic guidance utilizing Siemens Artis Q.zen angiography system.
3) Verapamil injected intra-arterially post procedure for prevention of radial artery spasm along with application of TR Band compression device post sheath removal.

1) Complete occlusion mid Left Anterior Descending artery(LAD).
2) Successful deployment drug-eluting stent(Xience Alpine Everolimus Eluting Coronary Stent System - Serial AB-1234567).

Post PCI care included transfer to Coronary Care Unit(CCU), initiation dual antiplatelet therapy(aspirin+ticagrelor). Mr. Novak reported experiencing severe chest pain radiating to his left arm for the past hour. The pain started while he was resting at home and was not relieved by nitroglycerin tablets. Upon arrival at the hospital, he was immediately assessed by Dr. Haruki Sato.

An ECG revealed ST-segment elevations in leads V1-V4, indicating an anterior wall STEMI. Mr. Novak was taken to the catheterization lab for an urgent coronary angiogram and possible PCI.

During the procedure:
1. A 6-French sheath was inserted into the right femoral artery.
2. A Judkins left catheter was used to engage the left main coronary artery.
3. Angiography revealed a total occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) artery.
4. A guidewire was passed through the lesion followed by balloon angioplasty with a Trek Rx Coronary Dilatation Catheter (2x15 mm).
5. A drug-eluting stent (Xience Sierra Everolimus Eluting Coronary Stent System [3x18 mm]) successfully restored flow in LAD without complications.

Mr. Novak tolerated the procedure well and remained hemodynamically stable throughout its duration.

Post-procedure medications:
- Aspirin
- Clopidogrel
- Atorvastatin
- Lisinopril
- Metoprolol tartrate

He will be monitored overnight in ICU before transferring to telemetry floor for further recovery until discharge planning is complete.

Follow-up appointments scheduled with:
1) Interventional Cardiologist Dr Sato - one week post-discharge 
2) Diabetes management: Endocrinologist Dr Anita Menon - two weeks post-discharge

Discharge instructions included cardiac rehabilitation referral information along with dietary education materials emphasizing low-fat/low-sodium diet plans tailored specifically for diabetic patients post myocardial infarction events like Mr.Novak's case scenario.

4. Consultation with electrophysiology team for possible cardioversion

1. Outpatient cardiology visit with Dr. Yamada on September 15th
2. Cardiac rehab intake evaluation on September 20th

Family members were also encouraged to access educational materials related to supporting loved ones after a heart attack at www.cardiosmart.org/postmi.

He was found to have an irregular pulse, and an ECG confirmed the diagnosis of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. 

Mr. Novak's contact information:
Address: 246 Maple Drive, Chicago, IL 60611
Phone: (312) 555-2468
Email: liam.novak@email.com
Medical Record Number: NMH-87654321

He was admitted under the care of Dr. Amir Patel who initiated treatment with intravenous diltiazem for rate control and apixaban for anticoagulation. A transthoracic echocardiogram showed moderate left atrial dilation but no valvular abnormalities or thrombus.

Due to Mr. Novak's active lifestyle and persistent symptoms despite medical therapy, the decision was made to proceed with catheter ablation for rhythm control on September 7th by Dr. Susan Lee. The procedure was performed using the CARTO® 3 System (Biosense Webster Inc.) which created a detailed electroanatomical map of his left atrium.

During his hospital stay, Mr. Novak received education about managing his diabetes and hypertension from Nurse Educator Maria Gonzalez RN CDE via https://nmhheartcenter.org/afibandeducation.

He tolerated the procedure well without complications and reverted to normal sinus rhythm prior to discharge on September 9th on oral diltiazem and apixaban therapy.

Follow up appointments were scheduled:
1) Wound check at Arrhythmia Clinic on September 14th
2) Cardiology consultation with Dr Amir Patel in four weeks 
3) Diabetes management follow-up in six weeks

Discharge instructions advised him to avoid heavy lifting or strenuous activity for two weeks post-ablation.

- White blood cell count: 12,000/mm³ (elevated)
- C-reactive protein: 35 mg/L (elevated)

The colonoscopy revealed multiple ulcerations and inflammation in the terminal ileum and ascending colon, consistent with a diagnosis of Crohn's disease.

2. Prednisolone was prescribed at an initial dose of 40 mg daily for two weeks, followed by tapering over six weeks.
3. Intravenous iron sucrose infusion was administered due to her iron deficiency anemia secondary to chronic blood loss from intestinal inflammation.
4. A referral was made to a dietitian for education on dietary modifications suitable for Crohn's disease management.

Follow-up Appointment:
A follow-up appointment has been scheduled in four weeks to assess response to treatment and adjust therapy as needed.

Upon arrival at the hospital, Mr. Novak underwent a comprehensive evaluation by Dr. Amir Patel and his team. Due to the severity of his condition and evidence of multivessel coronary artery disease from previous angiograms done at an outside facility on August 28th that showed significant stenoses in the left anterior descending (LAD), circumflex (Cx), and right coronary artery (RCA), it was decided that Mr. Novak would benefit from coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

On September 7th Dr. Olivia Larsson performed CABG x3 using a Medtronic cardiopulmonary bypass machine with an Inspire oxygenator system along with saphenous vein grafts for RCA and Cx territories while a left internal mammary artery (LIMA) graft was used for LAD territory.

Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography confirmed good biventricular function post-bypass; flow measurements in all grafts were satisfactory.

Mr. Novak's recovery was uneventful; he was extubated within 6 hours postoperatively and transferred to the step-down unit on postoperative day one where he continued to improve under telemetric monitoring.

Discharge medications included aspirin, metoprolol tartrate for heart rate control as needed targeting HR <70 bpm; lisinopril for blood pressure control targeting SBP <130 mmHg; atorvastatin for cholesterol management; oxycodone as needed for incisional pain not relieved by acetaminophen or ibuprofen.

He is scheduled to follow-up with Dr. Patel two weeks after discharge in his office located at Weill Cornell Medical Associates - Cardiology Clinic on East 72nd Street.

A referral has been made to cardiac rehabilitation services near Mr.Novak’s residence with instructions provided regarding dietary restrictions low in saturated fats emphasizing whole grains lean proteins fruits vegetables & importance of daily exercise starting gradually & increasing as tolerated.

2. Diet was gradually advanced from clear liquids to a regular diet as tolerated.
3. Mr Novak received education on signs and symptoms of recurrent small bowel obstruction and when to seek medical attention in the future.

3. Statin therapy with atorvastatin
4. ACE inhibitor therapy with lisinopril

Mr. Novak was monitored in the coronary care unit for two days before being transferred to a telemetry floor for continued recovery and education on lifestyle modifications.

He was discharged on September 10, instructed to follow up with his cardiologist Dr. Emily Choi within one week via telemedicine through NMH's MyChart patient portal: https://www.nm.org/mychart-login

HPI: Mr. Novak reported no recent changes in diet or travel history. He denied any fever or chills but did endorse anorexia due to the severity of his symptoms. His last bowel movement was on the morning of admission, which was normal in consistency.

Significant findings included tenderness and guarding in the right lower quadrant with rebound tenderness suggestive of acute appendicitis.

- C-reactive protein: Elevated at 85 mg/L

Mr. Novak underwent a laparoscopic appendectomy later that evening by Dr. Amirah Jalil without complications.

He tolerated the procedure well and his diet was advanced as tolerated post-operatively from clear liquids to a regular diet over the next day.
Pain management consisted of acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed.
Mr. Novak's condition improved significantly after surgery; he had no fever overnight and his pain decreased markedly.
He will follow up with Dr Amirah Jalil one week post discharge for wound check.

Disposition:
Liam Novak is discharged home on September 7th in stable condition with oral analgesics prescribed for pain control.

Mr. David Okafor, a 58-year-old man, was brought to the Emergency Department of Northwestern Memorial Hospital on June 8, 2023. He resides at 246 Elm Street, Chicago, IL 60611. Contact number: (312) 555-2468. His Medical Record Number is NMH-98765432.

The patient presented with severe abdominal pain that started approximately six hours before admission. The pain was localized in the upper right quadrant and was described as sharp and constant.

Examination revealed tenderness in the right upper quadrant with guarding. Murphy's sign was positive.

Laboratory tests showed elevated white blood cell count (14,000/mm³) and abnormal liver function tests with an alanine transaminase (ALT) of 150 U/L and an aspartate aminotransferase (AST) of 140 U/L.

An abdominal ultrasound demonstrated cholecystitis with thickening of the gallbladder wall and presence of gallstones.

The diagnosis of acute calculous cholecystitis was established by Dr. Michael Lee, attending surgeon at Northwestern Memorial Hospital.

Mr. Okafor underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy on June 9, which successfully alleviated his symptoms without complications during surgery.

Postoperative care instructions were provided via https://patient.nm.org/recoveryinstructions including information about wound care and activity restrictions for the next four weeks following surgery to ensure proper healing.

A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for June 23 with Dr. Lee through https://schedule.nm.org/ to assess recovery progress.

On September 5, 2023, Liam Novak, a 57-year-old male, was admitted to the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, MN. His Medical Record Number is MC-1029384756. After experiencing persistent abdominal pain and unintentional weight loss over the past two months, Mr. Novak underwent a series of diagnostic tests.

The gastroenterology team, led by Dr. Priya Singh, performed an upper endoscopy and colonoscopy on September 7, 2023. The biopsy results indicated adenocarcinoma of the stomach. Following these findings, a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis was conducted to stage the cancer.

Mr. Novak was diagnosed with stage III gastric cancer (T3N2M0). The multidisciplinary tumor board discussed his case and recommended neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgical resection.

He received four cycles of FOLFOX (5-fluorouracil/leucovorin/oxaliplatin) chemotherapy from October to December 2023 at Mayo Clinic's Oncology Department under the supervision of Dr. Ethan Kim.

On January 15th, 2024 Mr. Novak underwent a successful subtotal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy performed by Dr. Ava Sørensen at Mayo Clinic's Surgical Oncology Department.

Postoperatively he recovered well without complications and was discharged on January 22nd with comprehensive instructions for dietary adjustments and follow-up care provided through Mayo Clinic's online patient portal: https://connect.mayoclinic.org/

A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for February 12th with both Drs Singh & Kim to assess his recovery progress as well as discuss potential adjuvant treatment options based on final pathology results.

On September 5, 2023, Liam Novak, a 28-year-old male patient, presented to the Emergency Department at UCLA Medical Center with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. The patient's contact information is as follows: email - liam.n@email.com, phone - (310) 555-9876. Home address: 246 Sunset Blvd., Los Angeles, CA 90024.

HPI: Mr. Novak reported sudden onset of severe abdominal pain in the lower right quadrant approximately six hours prior to admission. He also experienced nausea and vomiting three times since the onset of pain. No recent changes in diet or similar episodes in the past.

PE: Physical examination revealed rebound tenderness and guarding in the lower right abdomen, suggestive of acute appendicitis. Vital signs were within normal limits except for a mildly elevated temperature at 99.8°F.

Dx: Acute appendicitis

Tx: The patient was taken to the operating room for an emergency laparoscopic appendectomy using a Stryker MiniLap™ system (Serial No.: STRY123456). The surgery was performed by Dr. Amit Patel without complications.

Postoperative care instructions were provided along with prescriptions for antibiotics and pain management medications. A follow-up appointment was scheduled with Dr. Patel on September 12, 2023.

Patient education materials regarding post-operative care and recovery from laparoscopic procedures were provided via UCLA Health's online portal at https://www.uclahealth.org/yourguide/postsurgerycare/.
